newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria third force ends support for Socialists.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria third force ends support for Socialists.

text.p: Bulgaria's third political force, the Bulgarian Business Bloc, has withdrawn parliamentary support for the ruling Socialists, who are under pressure to hold early elections.
"We will not support a cabinet proposed by the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) because the Socialists' economic policy has proven to be wrong," said BBB leader George Ganchev.
"The BSP has once again placed narrow party interests over national ones," he told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
After nine consecutive days of street protests, the Socialists said on Wednesday that elections could be held at the end of 1997, a year before their mandate expires.
Ganchev said the BBB planned to propose that political parties start talks on formation of a non-party caretaker government.

He said the BBB, which has traditionally attracted protest votes from people disillusioned with the two main parties, would not seek a coalition with any of the parties represented in the current parliament.
In November's presidential election, won by opposition lawyer Petar Stoyanov with 60 percent of the vote, Ganchev came third with almost 22 percent of the votes, close behind the Socialist candidate.

A former emigre who spent many years in the United States and formerly held U.S. citizenship, he describes himself as a centre-rightist but his party frequently votes with the Socialists in parliament.
The opposition walked out of parliament on Friday and pledged not to return until their demands for early general elections were met.

BBB spokesman Hristo Ivanov said the caretaker government should continue negotiations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on the implementation of a strict fixed exchange rate regime to stabilise the collapsing national currency.
He said it should introduce a more realistic 1997 budget bill than the one drawn up by the outgoing cabinet, and guarantee the country's grain balance for the next two years.
Ganchev said his party would not support an interim government, adding that the IMF would not agree long-term reform and funding measures with a government which is in power for two or three months.
"After elections I guarantee 40 to 45 seats for the Business Bloc in the new parliament," said Ganchev.
"We will hold the balance of power in the next parliament."
The BBB now holds 13 of parliament's 240 seats.
